boundary_evidence: NOT FROM tu_map. tools/tu_map.py reports the arm9 `main` module as UNDER-SEGMENTED: one unit 0x20049f0..0x20707a4 carrying 2984 functions and 73 class labels, because the module's class address-spans interleave and cluster() unions them all. There is no tu_map boundary here and no `tubuild.py create` candidate id; every line below is hand-derived and independently checkable.

contiguous linker run 0x02013e80..0x02013f28: the five functions tile the span exactly -- 0x24+0x38+0xc+0xc+0x34 = 0xa8 = end-start -- with no hole and no tail (recomputed from config/arm9/symbols.txt, not asserted).
no foreign symbol inside the span: config/arm9/symbols.txt lists exactly these five function symbols in [0x02013e80,0x02013f28) and nothing else.

class-label homogeneity: 4 of the 5 carry the _ZN7dBase_c prefix. The fifth, func_02013edc, is unnamed and is ENCLOSED by named members on both sides (D0 ends at it, Spawn begins after it), so no cut can exclude it without splitting the class's own run.

the run is the class's WHOLE run: grep of every config/**/symbols.txt in the image finds exactly four _ZN7dBase_c* function symbols and they are the four here. The class has no code anywhere else, so no competing span exists.

neighbour below: func_02013e64 (0x02013e64..0x02013e80), and the six functions before it are all _ZN8SaveData* (0x02013cd4..0x02013e64) -- a different class. Neighbour above: func_02013f28 (0x02013f28..0x02013f4c) then func_02013f4c. Both neighbours carry a different label from this run, so the run is bracketed rather than merely cut out of a uniform stretch.

key-function corroboration: ActorDerived declares exactly two virtuals of its own -- the destructor, defined INLINE in the header, and AfterInitResources. AfterInitResources is therefore the key function, and MEASURED HERE, defining it as a real method emits _ZTV7dBase_c and pulls the destructor's two vague-linkage out-of-line copies into existence for free (5/5 MATCH, no forcing scaffold). That is a direct demonstration that D1, D0 and AfterInitResources belong to ONE translation unit: compiling the key function is what makes the two destructor bodies exist at all, and it produces them in the ROM's own order. The shipped file then spells all three as extern "C" instead, because the emitted vtable collides with the gap object's copy and blocks the link -- but the boundary evidence stands on the first measurement, not on the workaround.

destructor-variant order corroborates the source form independently of any of the above. mwcc emits an OUT-OF-LINE destructor definition as the fixed group D2,D0,D1 (notes/tu-reconstruction-pilot-report.md sec 3), and ActorBase -- destructor defined out of line -- has exactly that in the ROM (0x02043d48 D2, 0x02043d78 D0, 0x02043dbc D1). An INLINE destructor's vague-linkage copies come out D1-then-D0 with no D2, which is what the pilot measured for Platform. This class has D1 (0x02013e80) then D0 (0x02013ea4) and no D2 anywhere in the image -- matching the inline form include/ActorDerived.h documents, and NOT matching a second out-of-line definition.

static-initialiser attribution: NO HELP, stated rather than skipped. build/tu_map.json gives main 23 sinits / 23 .ctor entries with sinit_vs_tu 'ok' but corroborated=false, and nothing in this run touches dynamically-initialised static storage, so no sinit can be pinned to it. This boundary rests on the four lines above, not on sinit counting.
notes: Hand-assembled, not generated by `tubuild.py create`: tu_map cannot segment arm9/main (see boundary_evidence line 1), so there was no candidate id to create from. The manifest entry was still built through tubuild.build_manifest_entry so the schema is the tool's own; boundary_confidence and boundary_evidence were then replaced with hand-derived values, because the tool's generated lines cite a tu_map unit that does not describe this run.

NEITHER OF THE CLASS'S OWN VIRTUALS IS DEFINED AS A METHOD HERE, deliberately. AfterInitResources is the key function (the only non-inline virtual ActorDerived declares), so a real method definition emits _ZTV7dBase_c, which collides with the module gap object's copy of the ROM vtable: the link aborts with 'Multiply-defined: virtual table for ActorDerived ... Previously defined in _dsd_gap@main_44.o'. Both forms were measured. Method form: 5/5 MATCH, 5 unlicensed .data symbols, link ABORTS. extern "C" form (shipped): 5/5 MATCH, 0 unlicensed anything, LINK-VERIFIED with the 168-byte range IDENTICAL. The class declarations in include/ActorDerived.h are untouched -- they are what give the class its slots.

The destructor's out-of-line copies are spelled directly under their mangled names rather than forced into existence by a scaffold. A never-called `p->~ActorDerived()` (what src/game/actors/dBase_c/_ZN7dBase_cD1Ev.cpp uses) is .text that no symbols.txt entry names: objisolate strips it per function, but a merged object cannot be reduced that way, `-nodead` keeps it, and it would land inside this span. include/ActorDerived.h's inline definition of ~ActorDerived is UNCHANGED and still load-bearing for Scene, Stage and every actor destructor below them.

_ZN7dBase_cD2Ev does not exist in the ROM and is not emitted here -- an inline destructor's vague-linkage copies are D1 and D0 only, which is itself the evidence that the header's inline definition is the right source form. ActorBase, whose destructor IS out of line, has the full D2,D0,D1 group at 0x02043d48/0x02043d78/0x02043dbc.
